column4: For every positive integer n, find a prime strictly between consecutive squares. A finite primality sweep cannot control all intervals; Bertrand's factor-two interval is too long. No uniform short-interval mechanism established.

Quantifier is limiting natural density of reciprocal-series coefficients over F2. Divisor notation is corrupted and f(0) is unspecified; invertibility requires constant coefficient 1. Do not silently supply it or infer density from a prefix.

Uniformly convergent sequence of subharmonic functions; ask whether other negative components hit every horizontal line. Unit-square convention conflicts with displayed [-1,1] coordinates, and eventual/all-k quantifier needs source. Uniform convergence confines extra components near x=0 but does not forbid thin channels.

For every linearly nondegenerate entire curve and general-position point system, total point defect at most one. Point defect needs exact counting convention. Hyperplane second-main-theorem bounds do not directly give this codimension-two constant; no local certificate.

All reciprocal rectangles simultaneously in one square; finite packings or total area one do not give compatible infinite placements. Tail area 1/(N+1) is necessary bookkeeping only. No full-scope constructive placement found.

General log-concave probability measures and conditioned Brownian motion on convex bodies. Curvature depends on the transition kernel, time and metric; nonnegative Hessian coupling alone does not answer all conditioned-process cases. Open-ended request lacks one exact endpoint.

All spaces with locally positive coarse curvature and global infimum zero; asks systematic relation to isoperimetry, plus M/M/k example. Metric/kernel/rate normalization and target bound absent. Queue instance cannot settle a universal characterization.

Every real dimension s in [1,2) for convex-billiard caustics and every s>=1 for Riemannian point caustics. A fractal invariant set is not automatically a caustic with requested regularity. No construction meeting both universal clauses.

Two separate all-period/all-polygon assertions. Rational-angle polygon unfolding only treats a subclass; finite-period checks cannot prove nowhere density for every n. No full-scope route to both clauses.

All admissible matrix pairs with common spectral radius and ordered dimension-module subquotient condition. Nonnegative adjacency convention and closed ordered submodule must be recovered; trace support is weaker than a factor construction. No bounded matrix test settles arbitrary sizes.

For every pair of mixing SFTs, all sufficiently large i,j should admit commuting realizations. Common underlying space and allowed conjugacies must be fixed. Comparing powers numerically cannot construct commuting actions.

Uniqueness among full-support invariant ergodic probability measures for the Section14 symbolic system, not arbitrary shifts. X and the full acting group are absent; Bernoulli measures on a guessed shift would be an invalid counterexample.

All surjective one-dimensional CA, with nu defined only through Question25.3, should satisfy nu>=sqrt(N). Missing definition of nu precludes a literal finite test. Surjectivity alone supplies no claimed periodic-point exponential bound.

Characterize countable G satisfying injective-implies-surjective for every finite alphabet and equivariant CA. Finite or residually finite cases cannot characterize arbitrary groups. No obstruction or full classification mechanism.

Every smooth planar F with a fixed point and rho(|DF(x)|)<1 everywhere should be globally asymptotically stable. Absolute-value matrix convention matters. Pointwise contractivity in varying weighted norms does not supply one uniform global contraction; no rigorous escaping orbit constructed.

All decimal integers should have multiplicative persistence <=11 under least-positive stabilization convention. Removing 0 and 1 digits reduces search but leaves unbounded prime-exponent triples. No finite bound reduction; no sweep attempted.

Infinitely many non-palindrome-reaching reverse-add starts and minimal such start 196. Long finite trajectories cannot certify nontermination; terminal palindrome search below 196 cannot establish the infinite-orbit clause.

For every positive-measure A and intersective polynomial family, some positive n gives simultaneous recurrence. Commutation and jointly-versus-separately intersective conventions are essential. Finite cyclic obstructions with incompatible roots would test a weaker misreading, not the source assertion.

For all invertible measure-preserving transformations, positive-measure A and distinct zero-constant integer polynomials, find common m,n. No commutation is stated. Standard commuting polynomial recurrence cannot be imported without a bridge.

Every distinct positive noninteger a,b and ergodic system, bounded f,g: almost-everywhere fractional-power averages equal product integrals. L2 convergence is insufficient for pointwise assertion; no maximal-inequality mechanism proved.

Almost surely universally over systems and bounded functions, random-time double averages converge in L2 or pointwise to product conditional expectations. Laws of a_n,b_n and independence are missing; L2 and pointwise are distinct endpoints.

Characterize convergence of pullback rational and coordinate maps for arbitrary branched coverings with three basepoints. Markings, normalization and convergence domains required. Critically finite Thurston theory does not characterize the noncritically-finite scope.

Every neighborhood of every Cremer point of every rational map should contain infinitely many periodic orbits. Density of repelling periodic points in Julia set does not show entire periodic orbits stay in the neighborhood. No small-cycle construction.

All real quadratic parameters in [-2,1/4], including infinitely renormalizable maps, have locally connected Julia sets. Nonrenormalizable/local special cases do not settle all c. Long renormalization dependency burden; no new elementary route.

Existence of a domain of uniform convergence of iterates to irrationally indifferent fixed point. Domain may exclude fixed point and germ iterates require continued definition. Derivative modulus one only obstructs domains containing a neighborhood of the fixed point, not the full question.

For every degree, hyperbolicity dense in full rational and polynomial parameter spaces. Real-parameter results or individual perturbations cannot cover complex parameter spaces. No full-scope perturbation scheme.

All explicitly specified smooth sphere diffeomorphisms and requested families: entropy computable to any error and useful time; also metric entropy in area-preserving cases. Representation and useful-time bound absent; Hénon/standard map domains require reconciliation.

Every closed polyhedron admits a connected nonoverlapping general unfolding. Edge or vertex unfolding examples do not answer arbitrary surface cuts. Surface topology and allowed disconnected vertex neighborhoods need primary conventions; no finite universal cut algorithm.

Every arbitrary polygon should reach a regular one after finitely many one-vertex translations along its current centroid line. Need simple-polygon and intermediate-degeneracy conventions. Linear rank/invertibility of individual updates alone does not generate all target configurations; inspect primary before a control calculation.

Yao-Yao graph should have a constant stretch bound for all node sets. Cone count, incoming-edge pruning, ties and directed/undirected convention are absent ('See below'). Different cone counts have different behavior; cannot assign a single theorem without source.

Open-ended classification of boundaries from strict hyperbolization, not a single universal equation. Need Charney-Davis construction and desired invariant. A single computable boundary is not full-scope resolution.

Every minimal convergence action on compact metrizable Z should extend to uniformly quasi-isometric quasi-action on hyperbolic X with boundary Z. 'Topologically transitive' is defined here as every orbit dense (minimal). Known special geometrically finite actions do not supply all actions.

Existence of exotic homology manifolds 'as in [14]' as Coxeter ideal boundaries. Reference defines exotic class and geometry needed; arbitrary homology-sphere examples do not meet it. No exact construction proposed.

Boundary equality of Coxeter constructions from flag triangulated closed3-manifolds should force equality of prime summands, plus higher-dimensional inquiry. C(N,Delta), equality/homeomorphism and index Ni+1 conventions need source; cannot infer rigidity from a guessed construction.

Every group Z-boundary compactum should fail Boltyansky dimension drop. Standard check is dim(ZxZ)<2dim(Z); requires finite-dimensional/convention hypotheses. Equal-block Markov case is explicitly already proved, so extending only it earns no credit.

All one-ended CAT(0) groups: does local connectedness imply boundary uniqueness? Visual-boundary homeomorphism versus equivariant uniqueness must be fixed. Existing badly nonlocally connected examples cannot simply be repurposed.

Every quasiconformal ball homeomorphism should be approximable by global QC diffeomorphisms, optionally common K. Topology, dimension and K dependence unspecified; smoothing coordinate charts does not preserve a uniform distortion bound automatically.

Every hyperbolic group should admit a discrete uniformly quasiconformal sphere action for some dimension. Embedding boundary into sphere is insufficient to extend the group action with uniform dilatation. No constructive full-group extension.

Circle-to-sphere equivariant Cannon-Thurston map for G from preceding source context; group/representation and Problem64 omitted. General subgroup formulation is separate388799; do not substitute it for this literal target.

Every hyperbolic subgroup of a hyperbolic group, without quasiconvexity, should admit a boundary map. A known-looking nonexistence construction is a prior-art objection requiring actual body confirmation; quasi-convex inclusion handles only a subclass. No new construction invested.

Identify Poisson boundary for every probability measure on a free group. Degenerate-support, moment and entropy cases differ; geometric boundary identification under finite-moment hypotheses does not cover arbitrary measures.

Almost-sure single horofunction attaining drift limit, stronger than separate epsilon horofunctions. Space/cocycle, integrability and stationarity hypotheses missing. Compactness of h_epsilon does not justify interchanging time and epsilon limits.

Every arithmetic lattice in real-hyperbolic Isom(H^n), n>=4, should contain a finitely generated non-finitely-presented subgroup. The trailing quaternionic property-T sentence is distinct context; no direct coherence implication. No full arithmetic-family mechanism.

All closed Y of dimension not4 admitting no positive scalar curvature should have bounded-width scalar-positive bands. n and ideal constant parsing need source context. Standard torical-band cases alone would be family instances.

Generic ambient Riemannian metrics should have nonsingular volume-minimizing hypersurfaces in arbitrary dimension. Generic topology, multiplicity and minimizer class need fixing; n=8 case is explicitly already reported. No arbitrary-dimension perturbation proof.

For CP2-type X and every tangent-nonspin surface S, all 0<delta<=1 have tubular volume>=delta²; infer spin-area>=10^-6. spin-area and T(X)-nonspin absent; 'homomorphic' cannot be silently corrected. No test on guessed metric.

Every manifold should immerse in Hilbert unit ball with one universal bound on principal curvatures. Metric prescribed versus induced, manifold dimension and infinite-codimension curvature convention are crucial. Coordinate sine embeddings do not give universal operator curvature automatically.

Every Q-essential n-pseudomanifold with arbitrary metric: for each radius a lifted ball reaches Euclidean Hilbert volume. Exact Hilbert volume and metric regularity are missing; arbitrary rescaling alone is not a counterexample because the small-scale volume normalization also changes.

All compact n-pseudomanifolds satisfying Hilbert-volume bounds for every small ball should have all low-Lipschitz sphere maps nullhomotopic. Strict inequality, constants and Hilbert-volume definition matter; Riemannian volume comparison cannot be substituted.

For every ell,k>0 choose uniform C,L,K for all complete manifolds with inj>=ell and Ric>=k, then a bilipschitz bounded-Ricci metric. Dimension dependence and tensor convention need source; smoothing under lower Ricci alone is not automatic. No compactness-based construction established.
